discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that time-reversal-invariant insulators carry a hidden Z2 topological invariant, predicting the quantum spin Hall state with protected helical edge channels. Molenkamp's group realized it in 2007 in HgTe quantum wells, observing quantized edge conductance near 2e^2/h that is independent of sample width, a decisive transport signature. These ideas were extended to three-dimensional topological insulators, now confirmed by ARPES, STM and transport in many laboratories. They opened a new classification of matter based on band topology rather than broken symmetry. This framework led directly to the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators, axion insulators, topological superconductivity and proposals for fault-tolerant quantum devices. A close dialogue between theory and patient materials work turned an abstract invariant into measurable, quantized physics, changing how condensed matter physicists think about electronic states in solids.
